title: Loss of plasticity in deep continual learning (arXiv precursor: Maintaining Plasticity in Deep Continual Learning)
low_dose_frontier_quality: rho=1e-4 sustains plasticity to 5000 tasks; too-large rho behaves like re-init
near_collapse_behaviour: accuracy falls 89% -> 77% (linear-net level) by task 2000; ~25% dead units and rising weight magnitude + falling effective rank accompany it
notes: Canonical evidence plasticity loss is real and gradual over long lineages; gives the three cheap diagnostics (dead-unit %, mean |w|, effective rank). L2 + shrink-and-perturb was best of the standard mitigations.

title: The Dormant Neuron Phenomenon in Deep Reinforcement Learning
low_dose_frontier_quality: tau=0.1 is the reported operating point; tau=0 finds only fully dead units and pruning them costs nothing
near_collapse_behaviour: dormant fraction rises ~5-10% -> 40-60% over 200M frames; ~70% at replay ratio 2.0; dormant units rarely reactivate on their own
notes: Best-specified cheap diagnostic with an actual threshold (tau=0.1 on layer-normalised mean activation). ReDo raised effective rank 449.2 -> 470.8 and gave ~15-25% score gains at RR=1.0.

title: Efficient transformer adaptation for analog in-memory computing via low-rank adapters
method_family: noise-aware training under injected Gaussian weight noise
utility_metric: HellaSwag acc / GSM8K CoT acc / SQuAD F1
low_dose_frontier_quality: 3.0% noise used for the harder RL/GSM8K run; 6.7% for instruction tuning
near_collapse_behaviour: LLaMA-3.1-8B at 6.7% weight noise drops HellaSwag 78.91% -> 29.48% and GSM8K 85.06% -> 37.98%; LoRA training UNDER that same noise recovers to 67.71% and 70.74%
notes: Closest direct test of H6: a model whose weights carry large persistent Gaussian noise and whose task accuracy has collapsed by ~47 points is still trainable, and gradient descent under the noise recovers most of the gap. Training destabilises entirely at ~12% noise.

title: On Warm-Starting Neural Network Training
low_dose_frontier_quality: lambda=0.6 with noise scale 0.01 matches fresh-init generalisation while keeping the warm-start speedup
near_collapse_behaviour: warm start alone loses 4.5pp (CIFAR-10 SGD 56.2 -> 51.7) and 6.4pp (CIFAR-100 Adam 41.4 -> 35.0) vs fresh init; shrinking + noising closes it
notes: Direct evidence that a deliberately shrunk-and-noised checkpoint trains FASTER than a fresh init and generalises as well - i.e. administered weight noise restores rather than destroys trainability. Same operator family as the decay arm.

title: Can Scale Save Us From Plasticity Loss in Large Language Models?
low_dose_frontier_quality: larger models delay but do not avoid onset; onset scales as T = 1.3e-5 * P^0.8269
near_collapse_behaviour: onset is sublinear in params; 27M model degrades after ~320B tokens continual vs ~475B stationary; single MLP layers reach >95% dormancy
notes: Only LLM-scale plasticity study found. Reports dormant-unit accumulation and attention-head pathologies (lazy head >90% max entropy, collapsed head <10%) but says none is a smoking gun - diagnostics are correlational, not predictive.

title: Revisiting BFloat16 Training
low_dose_frontier_quality: stochastic rounding lands within -0.1/+0.2% of fp32 across seven applications
near_collapse_behaviour: pure-bf16 nearest rounding of weight updates loses 8.6pp on ResNet-50 ImageNet (75.70 -> 67.10) and 6.82pp on BERT-MNLI (84.35 -> 77.53); small updates are silently cancelled
notes: Key precision risk for the merge-to-BF16-each-day design: any per-day update smaller than a BF16 ULP of the weight is discarded. Keep fp32 master weights during the forget/heal step and only cast at merge, or use stochastic rounding.

title: FIT to Forget: Robust Continual Unlearning for Large Language Models
method_family: sequential unlearning with layer attribution + adaptive method selection
low_dose_frontier_quality: 25% layer update ratio keeps utility while forgetting
near_collapse_behaviour: at 300 sequential requests Llama-3-8B holds F.D. 0.73 +/- 0.05 and R.U. 0.71 +/- 0.05 with MMLU 65.56 CSQA 70.01 GSM8K 57.02; ablating adaptive selection drops GSM8K to 14.12
notes: Strongest evidence the forgetting arm does not exhaust itself: 300 sequential erasures with stable forget quality. Note the forget arm survives because of targeted layer selection, not because naive sequential unlearning is safe (naive baselines collapse).

title: A Study of Plasticity Loss in On-Policy Deep Reinforcement Learning
low_dose_frontier_quality: soft shrink+perturb and L2-init were the consistent winners across shift types
near_collapse_behaviour: weight magnitude and dead-unit fraction correlate significantly with reward degradation (p<0.05); gradient norm does NOT in the on-policy setting; plasticity injection underperformed even the warm-start baseline
notes: Directly informs which diagnostics to log: mean |w| and dead-unit fraction predict; gradient norm and inter-update weight delta do not. Off-policy-derived fixes can be worse than nothing, so do not port ReDo blindly.

title: Maintaining Plasticity in Continual Learning via Regenerative Regularization
low_dose_frontier_quality: single hyperparameter; performs comparably to continual backprop
near_collapse_behaviour: regularising toward theta_0 rather than 0 keeps weight rank from collapsing; most consistent plasticity preservation across nonstationarity types
notes: Cheapest heal-arm insurance policy for a lineage: an L2-toward-day0-parent penalty during the healing fine-tune. Paper reports consistency across problem types rather than a single headline number.

title: Understanding plasticity in neural networks
utility_metric: plasticity (loss reduction on a fresh target)
low_dose_frontier_quality: layer norm and optimiser/parameterisation choices preserve plasticity
near_collapse_behaviour: plasticity loss is tied to loss-landscape curvature change and OFTEN OCCURS WITH NO SATURATED UNITS - dead-unit counts can look healthy while plasticity is already gone
notes: Important caveat for the diagnostic panel: dead-unit fraction and feature rank are not sufficient. Suggests adding a direct probe - measure loss reduction achievable on a fixed held-out fitting task each day.

title: Understanding and Preventing Capacity Loss in Reinforcement Learning
low_dose_frontier_quality: InFeR raises feature rank over the whole of training
near_collapse_behaviour: capacity loss - the network's ability to fit new targets - degrades under nonstationary targets and hurts most in sparse-reward tasks
notes: Origin of the 'effective/feature rank' diagnostic for nonstationary training. Mechanism is the same one the lineage faces: repeatedly refitting shifting targets.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning with Plasticity Injection
method_family: plasticity injection as a diagnostic intervention
near_collapse_behaviour: if adding fresh parameters mid-training improves performance, plasticity loss was the binding constraint
notes: Gives a decisive but expensive test rather than a cheap metric: on a suspect day, add fresh capacity (e.g. re-init a small adapter) and see if the day's erasure objective suddenly fits better. Use as a tiebreaker, not a daily log.
